what_happened: Job 20261107-031917-r96w ("Stop retrying a failing line and queue one diagnosis job", code) failed in planning, before any code was written. In round 1 of 5 the critic said the reading misread the request, and the plan then still needed revising at the last round. The request counts "attempts that do not land" and names "collision with another landing" as a failure category. The reading narrowed that to records that are Rejected or Failed. An attempt that passed verification but did not land (LandStep::NotLanded) counts only if its job closed with a non-landed outcome. If the job is still blocked or open, it is not counted, so a line could have two collisions and never be diagnosed. The critic also found four design problems. (1) The plan files the diagnosis invocation under the line's last job, which is already closed. That breaks the landing gate's check that a closed job's totals match its invocation records, and it inflates that job's spend and score. (2) The retry follow-up joins the original line. The core refuses both the reading and the dispatch when the scope guard has paused that line, which the plan's own risks call the usual case at two failures. (3) The collision gap above. (4) Every drain demonstration uses a fake that computes line standing itself, so the real drain step reading real records is never exercised, and the drain part of criterion 9 cannot fail. Minor findings: seven files outside the deliverables (most needed to compile), an unlisted exhaustive Role match in the CLI test fake, a request to "queue" a job that the plan runs inline with no job record, and a failed diagnosis that stays claimed until a local file is deleted by hand. No acceptance criteria were reported unmet and no checks failed. Nothing was delivered.
cause: Planning checks that the seams a plan names exist. It does not make the reading or plan trace each claim through the code that consumes it. Here those claims were what counts as "did not land", which invariant a closed job's invocation records must satisfy, and whether a paused line accepts a follow-up. Each of these could be settled by reading the gate, the scope guard and the drain. The reading narrowed a request term to a record status without checking how landing outcomes are recorded. The plan's tests use a fake that computes line standing itself, so its own demonstrations cannot expose any of these gaps. The change also touches a core flow, the drain, where the gate, scope guard and store interact. Planning has fixed rounds, keeps no partial plan and has no repair step for gaps the code can answer, so a major finding left at the last round loses all planning spend.
prevention: Give planning a code-answerable check before the critic rounds. For a change to a core flow, the planner must list each claim about existing behavior (what counts as an outcome, which records the gate reconciles, which states the scope guard refuses) and cite the code line that settles it. Open questions the code can answer are not allowed to remain. Require at least one demonstration per criterion to run the real step on real records instead of a fake that computes the answer. Add a repair round so a mechanical or code-answerable major finding at the last round gets one more revision instead of failing the job. Together these would have caught all four design problems before the critic's final round.
proposed_request: Stop retrying a failing line and queue one diagnosis job. When a line (a chain of a job and its retries/follow-ups) has two attempts that did not land, the drain should stop retrying it and start one diagnosis run, once per line. Attempts that did not land include: rejected, failed, and attempts that passed verification but could not land (collision with another landing), whether or not their job is still open or blocked. Outcomes: (1) A line with two such attempts of any category is diagnosed exactly once, and no further retry is queued for it. (2) The diagnosis run is recorded under its own fresh run id, as the steward does, not under the line's last closed job, so the landing gate's totals check for closed jobs still passes and that job's spend and score do not change. (3) The retry-on-new-code follow-up is allowed when the scope guard has paused the line, in both the reading step and dispatch, and a test shows it on a paused line. (4) At least one drain demonstration runs the real drain step over real records written by the real writers, including a collision attempt whose job is still open, and fails if the count or the once-only claim is wrong. (5) A failed diagnosis can be released or retried with an Athena command, not by deleting a local file. Allowed changes include diagnosis.rs, store.rs, reading.rs, run_pin_tests.rs, the fake agent, the CLI main.rs and tests/drain.rs, and the exhaustive Role matches that need the new variant. Read the code to settle how landing outcomes, the gate's reconcile check and the scope guard behave, and name the lines in the plan.
